we talked about this today 👀

evals should push the frontier of what agents are capable of doing -  things ppl aren’t doing today bc maybe the surface doesn’t yet exist

this is uniquely different from evals that map the “now” of the agent like regression test style evals

you often don’t have traces that represents the future looking behavior

the greatest product minds build on behalf of their user with radical clarity -> you’re also in a way building/eval’ing on behalf of your future users

for RL Tasks this is more clear - you shoot for a 0.2-0.6 pass rate so you have signal to climb on. but the same holds for evals that you never use for hill climbing

if you have a great internal world model for how ppl will use your agent - you can do a bunch without traces

but traces make that concrete bc no one has a perfect world model of real world usage

tldr: build evals for the frontier of where you want your agents to go
